decision: Return a canonical assessment binding inputs, policy, analyzers, findings, coverage, uncertainty, and gate verdict rather than a Boolean.
forcedBy: R-checkable; W-CI; W-human; unequal language depth
rejected: Boolean plus console messages, because it loses provenance and omitted work
Unstructured logs, because they are not a stable replayable machine contract
falsifiedBy: A Boolean/log design that preserves exact inputs, uncertainty, later explanation, machine consumption, and upgrade comparison without recreating an assessment elsewhere.

decision: Analyze an immutable logical snapshot of exact source, configuration, dependency, and declared environment inputs.
forcedBy: W-agent overlapping edits; R-checkable; W-CI reproducibility
rejected: Reading the live filesystem throughout a run, because inputs can drift
Using only a Git commit, because working-tree and other relevant inputs are omitted
Using timestamps as identity, because they do not identify content
falsifiedBy: A complete filesystem or VCS snapshot facility that already supplies an immutable reproducible view of every relevant input for a run.

decision: Make analyzers hermetic and deterministic: snapshot-only reads, no network/model/clock/random/ambient environment, and canonical enumeration and reduction.
forcedBy: R-offline; R-deterministic; R-checkable; W-CI
rejected: Best-effort offline execution, because external state can still change results
Behavioral documentation for plugins without enforcement, because it cannot uphold the product promise
Seeded nondeterminism, because clock, concurrency, and network inputs remain
falsifiedBy: A newly required result that inherently depends on live external state, or inability to enforce hermeticity on required platforms without an equivalent substitute.

decision: Canonicalize rule instances and identify all analyzer, schema, frontend, default, parameter, and data semantics as inputs.
forcedBy: Teams declare rules; R-checkable; R-adoption across upgrades
rejected: Hashing only user-written config, because expanded defaults and transitive packages disappear
A marketing version as semantic identity, because independently changing components are hidden
Analyzer-selected severity, because policy authority belongs to the team/core
falsifiedBy: A permanently monolithic build whose one immutable digest completely identifies every semantic component and policy expansion.

decision: Model facts, subjects, claims, evidence, coverage, findings, and verdict as separate objects, with the core owning final assessment.
forcedBy: Judgment; supported by W-human, R-extension, R-languages, and W-CI
rejected: A universal AST, because it loses language-specific semantics
Analyzer-emitted final diagnostics, because identity, evidence, baseline, and policy become inconsistent
One undifferentiated event log, because invariants become difficult to validate
falsifiedBy: A simpler model that supports deep heterogeneous analysis, extension authority, coverage, explanation, and upgrade comparison with less translation.

decision: Represent required analysis as satisfied, violated, not_applicable, or indeterminate with structured reason codes; never encode unknown as pass.
forcedBy: R-languages; explicit requirement to report what could not be determined; W-CI
rejected: Dropping failed or unsupported targets, because it creates false passes
Treating every unknown as a violation, because it misstates evidence
Warning-only logs, because CI can ignore them
falsifiedBy: Complete, terminating, sound analyzers for every requested language/rule with no missing inputs or operational failures.

decision: Publish versioned analyzer capabilities and require rules to declare capabilities so planning accounts for the complete target universe.
forcedBy: R-languages unequal breadth/depth; R-checkable
rejected: A binary supported-language flag, because it exaggerates shallow support
Running rules with missing semantics, because findings may be unsound
Silently excluding unsupported files, because it corrupts coverage
falsifiedBy: One sound uniform semantic representation that provides identical capabilities for every supported language.

decision: Attach to every finding a structured evidence witness linking source anchors, facts, producer provenance, rule predicates, and derivation edges.
forcedBy: The product must prove its answer; R-checkable; W-human
rejected: Message and line number only, because they are fragile and do not show derivation
Debug logs, because they do not define the justification
A rerun command alone, because historical inputs or implementation may be missing
falsifiedBy: Users require only analyzer identity/location, or practical formal proof certificates supersede evidence graphs for every analysis.

decision: Define canonical serialization and root identities so equal semantic inputs yield an equal assessment root and exit class.
forcedBy: R-deterministic; R-checkable; W-CI
rejected: Ordinary JSON byte comparison, because ordering and incidental metadata vary
Run UUIDs, because they identify executions rather than equivalence
Semantic timestamps/hostnames, because they harm replay and are irrelevant
falsifiedBy: A different stable offline equivalence protocol with collision-resistant input/result binding and no canonical root.

decision: Keep immutable result and baseline artifacts separate from disposable mutable acceleration caches.
forcedBy: R-checkable; R-adoption; W-agent and R-scale cache pressure
rejected: Using the latest cache database as history, because eviction/migration rewrites the record
Hosted-only reports, because hosted operation is optional
Console-only history, because it lacks structured closure
falsifiedBy: Acceleration state itself can be permanently immutable, portable, schema-stable, and inexpensive enough to remove the distinction.

decision: Store objects by domain-separated SHA-256 and support deterministic sealed bundles containing a report's complete replay closure.
forcedBy: Judgment; supported by R-scale, R-checkable, and R-adoption
rejected: A monolithic database, because partial export and corruption isolation are harder
Embedding all source in every report, because it scales poorly
Hashes without retained objects, because identity alone cannot replay
BLAKE3 initially, because SHA-256 has broader independent verifier availability
falsifiedBy: Measurements show CAS/SHA-256 overhead dominates, or a transactional pack provides equivalent immutable portable closure more simply.

decision: Record accepted debt as an immutable, policy-scoped source snapshot anchor plus reviewed result context, not as mutable suppressions.
forcedBy: Judgment under R-adoption
rejected: Analyzer fingerprint lists, because semantic upgrades make them stale
Source-line suppressions, because they can mask future instances and disperse policy
Automatic baseline replacement, because it destroys the gate
falsifiedBy: A version-independent finding identity has lower storage and no silent suppression, or retaining accepted source snapshots is unacceptable.

decision: On upgrade, evaluate accepted and current snapshots with the same current analyzer/rule semantics and compare those results; retain the historical result for audit.
forcedBy: Judgment under R-adoption trust across upgrades
rejected: Comparing old-engine baseline fingerprints with new-engine current fingerprints, because analyzer churn appears as code change
Permanently pinning the old engine, because fixes and new analysis cannot enter the gate
Fingerprint migration without replay, because correspondence is unproved
falsifiedBy: Replay remains too expensive after caching, accepted snapshots cannot be retained, or a version-independent proof identity exists for all rules.

decision: Use core-owned semantic lineage and multi-valued delta states; classify ambiguous correspondence as indeterminate rather than silently new or existing.
forcedBy: R-adoption trustworthiness across refactors and upgrades
rejected: Path-plus-line hashes, because line insertion breaks them
Message hashes, because presentation changes identity
Unqualified fuzzy matching, because heuristic confidence becomes gate authority
Extension-owned existing classification, because it can bypass policy
falsifiedBy: A complete version-independent identity follows every finding through arbitrary program transformations.

decision: Read old baseline schemas or migrate by emitting linked immutable objects; never mutate/reaccept automatically during upgrade.
forcedBy: R-adoption; R-checkable
rejected: In-place baseline database migrations, because they erase the old meaning
Regenerating incompatible baselines from current code, because new violations may be blessed
Best-effort partial parsing, because loss can be invisible
falsifiedBy: Cross-version acceptance compatibility is dropped as a requirement, or a universal immutable baseline schema never needs migration.

decision: Plan and execute a deterministic dependency DAG of discovery, semantic, rule, evidence, and delta tasks.
forcedBy: Judgment; supported by W-agent, R-scale, and shared deep-analysis intermediates
rejected: A monolithic full-repository pass for every query, because it wastes small-edit reuse
Independent passes per rule, because they duplicate parsing and resolution
An undeclared mutable object graph, because invalidation is hard to audit
falsifiedBy: Full runs meet interactive latency at 100,000 files, or a simpler streaming design provides better deterministic reuse.

decision: Key cached tasks by every semantic input and validate schemas so warm and cold assessments are identical.
forcedBy: Judgment to cache for W-agent/R-scale; complete keys then follow from R-deterministic/R-checkable
rejected: Path/mtime keys, because they miss content and configuration changes
Analyzer-version-only invalidation, because it is both coarse and incomplete
Unvalidated serialized extension data, because stale/corrupt data crosses trust boundaries
falsifiedBy: Complete keys cost more than recomputation, or an analyzer's true inputs cannot be declared and it must be non-cacheable.

decision: Provide one semantic engine in a mandatory one-shot path and an optional workspace-local resident path; daemon absence falls back to one-shot.
forcedBy: W-CI forces one-shot; daemon is judgment for W-agent and R-scale
rejected: A mandatory local/remote service, because it violates no-service operation and CI shape
One-shot only without measurement, because repeated cold costs may harm the dominant workload
Separate daemon and CI semantics, because results could drift
falsifiedBy: One-shot latency meets the dominant workload, or daemon lifecycle/security costs exceed reuse benefits.

decision: Give each overlapping query its own snapshot while coalescing only identical immutable task keys with reference-counted cancellation.
forcedBy: Judgment for W-agent while preserving snapshot/reproducibility invariants
rejected: One mutable latest-project graph, because request states can mix
Serializing all checks, because overlap is wasted
First-client cancellation of shared work, because timing changes other results
falsifiedBy: Measured overlap is rare, or a transactional mutable index demonstrates simpler equivalent isolation.

decision: For small checks, compute and report a conservative impact closure; widen or mark gaps indeterminate, and reserve repository-wide claims for full checks.
forcedBy: W-agent small queries; R-checkable; deep transitive analyses; R-scale
rejected: Edited-lines-only checks, because effects propagate
Always-full checks, because they may defeat rapid interaction at scale
Unreported heuristic scopes, because clean results become uncheckable
falsifiedBy: All rules are file-local, or full analysis at maximum scale always meets interactive latency.

decision: Specify deterministic parallel reductions and treat declared resource-limit exhaustion as indeterminate rather than truncated success.
forcedBy: R-scale; R-deterministic; W-CI; finite offline laptop resources
rejected: Race-dependent first-result behavior, because load changes output
Undeclared wall-clock timeouts, because replay differs
Unlimited execution, because checks can hang
Silent truncation, because it creates false confidence
falsifiedBy: All analyses terminate in fixed negligible bounds and serial execution meets scale requirements.

decision: Run heavy language engines in supervised bounded local workers and localize their failures to affected coverage cells.
forcedBy: Judgment; supported by heterogeneous frontends, W-agent residency, and explicit uncertainty
rejected: All frontends in the core process, because crash and heap retention domains expand
A process per file, because startup cost is excessive
Abort-all on one parser failure, because useful evidence is discarded
falsifiedBy: In-process engines are materially faster and sufficiently safe, or IPC/serialization dominates.

decision: Initially expose bounded declarative rule packages over versioned facts; admit new executable fact producers only through trusted review and pinned releases.
forcedBy: Judgment under R-extension, constrained by R-deterministic, R-offline, and no inference
rejected: Native runtime plugins, because portable hermetic enforcement is weak
General WASM initially, because arbitrary embedded inference and evidence/resource validation remain
No extensions, because common organization-specific rules would be excluded
falsifiedBy: Real rule demand exceeds the declarative language and a portable certified executable sandbox enforces all product guarantees.

decision: Limit extensions to candidate facts/claims; core owns baseline lineage, uncertainty, policy, provenance, canonical result, and exit status; lock packages by digest.
forcedBy: R-deterministic; R-checkable; R-adoption; W-CI
rejected: Package names/version ranges, because identical config can resolve differently
Plugin-emitted final reports, because schemas and gate semantics fragment
Runtime latest-package resolution, because it violates offline reproducibility
falsifiedBy: Extensions are removed, or an attestable runtime safely delegates these authorities with equivalent core enforcement.

decision: Separate logical verdict, completeness, and operational health; map exits to 0 pass, 1 proved policy failure, 2 required indeterminacy, 3 invocation/config error, 4 core failure, and 130 interruption.
forcedBy: W-CI and explicit unknown reporting force separation/nonzero behavior; exact mapping is judgment
rejected: One nonzero code for all cases, because violation and tool failure are indistinguishable
Bitmask exits, because shell use is awkward and rich detail still needs the report
Zero plus warnings for incomplete work, because it creates false passes
falsifiedBy: Target CI platforms impose another convention, or research shows bitmask/sysexits behavior is materially less error-prone.

decision: Implement the trusted core, CLI, daemon, scheduler, storage, policy, evidence, baseline, and supervision layers in Rust.
forcedBy: Judgment; supported by offline distribution, R-scale, safe concurrency, and controlled runtime
rejected: Go for now, because Rust offers more memory/layout control, though Go remains viable
C++, because memory-safety burden is larger
TypeScript/Python core, because runtime packaging, cold start, and memory are concerns
JVM core, because it enlarges deployment assumptions
falsifiedBy: Team expertise/ecosystem makes another language safer or faster, profiling removes runtime concerns, or Rust platform distribution is worse.

decision: Choose TypeScript/JavaScript and Python as the initial two deep language families, subject to corpus validation.
forcedBy: R-languages specifies two but supplies no corpus, customer, rule-demand, staffing, licensing, or platform evidence
rejected: Rust, Java/Kotlin, C/C++, C#, and Go, because none can be ranked from the prompt
Choosing Rust merely to match the core, because symmetry is not a requirement
Claiming more than two initially, because depth staffing is unknown
falsifiedBy: Customer corpus/rule demand ranks a different pair, or frontend licensing/distribution/determinism blocks either choice.

decision: Support additional languages through pinned capability-graded adapters and retain language-specific semantic fact namespaces.
forcedBy: Judgment under R-languages breadth with unequal depth
rejected: One universal AST, because semantics are lost and rules overclaim
Unlabeled regex support, because it misrepresents capability
Deep bespoke frontends for every language, because it conflicts with the two-language depth focus
falsifiedBy: A common semantic IR is faithful and affordable across target languages, or users define support only as deep compiler analysis.

decision: Ship a self-sufficient local distribution; CI uses the same one-shot engine; hosted systems may only ingest/render canonical artifacts and never affect results.
forcedBy: R-offline; R-hosted-optional; W-CI
rejected: Remote analysis or cloud cache in the correctness path, because external state affects results
Hosted-only baselines, because offline net-new gating fails
Separate cloud analyzer semantics, because local and hosted verdicts can drift
falsifiedBy: Requirements change to mandate centrally computed results or accept loss of offline reproducible operation.

decision: Require content integrity for baselines but make reviewer cryptographic signatures optional until an authorization threat model exists.
forcedBy: No attacker, key infrastructure, branch protection, or acceptance-authority requirement is given
rejected: Mandatory signatures, because key management is unjustified without a threat model
No integrity binding, because accidental mutation would be invisible
falsifiedBy: Contributors must be unable to alter accepted state without designated approval, or enterprise requirements mandate signed provenance.
